## 2026-08-11 Plan to import from analytics-and-big-data

::: {.callout-tip title="Import plan" collapse=true}

Import the relevant source materials unchanged as a migration baseline, then recompose the course section-by-section.
Keep the existing `machine-learning-for-big-data` session structure, `course.yml`, styling, and session paths authoritative.
Separate structural migration, Python-to-R conversion, and content revision into distinct stages.

### Stage 1: Import source materials

Copy the relevant materials from `analytics-and-big-data` unchanged:

- slides
- exercises
- teaching notes
- required datasets
- referenced images/includes
- bibliography entries

Record the source repository and commit SHA in `changelog.qmd`.

Commit separately:

```text
Import teaching materials from analytics-and-big-data
```

### Stage 2: Recompose into MLBD sessions

Map and rename the imported materials according to the target syllabus:

| Target session         | Main source                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| 1: Big Data            | Lecture 8 + parts of Lecture 1 |
| 1: Basics in R         | Create anew                    |
| 2: Analytics           | Lecture 1                      |
| 2: Data Preparation    | Lecture 2 + Exercise 2         |
| 3: EDA                 | Lecture 2 + Exercise 2         |
| 4: Regression          | Lecture 4 + Exercise 4         |
| 5: Classification      | Lecture 5 + Exercise 5         |
| 6: ML Workflow         | Lecture 6                      |
| 7: ML Algorithms       | Lecture 7                      |
| 8: Text                | Lecture 8 + Exercise 8         |
| 9: Image, Video, Audio | Lecture 9 + Exercise 9         |
| 9: Deployment          | Lecture 10 + Exercise 10       |

At this stage, retain Python examples unchanged.

### Stage 3: Port session-by-session to R

Work through each session:

```text
slides/session_XX.qmd
exercises/session_XX.qmd
notes/session_XX.qmd
data/assets
```

For each session:

- convert Python/pandas/scikit-learn examples to R;
- use `tidyverse` and `tidymodels` where appropriate;
- update exercises and solutions;
- update teaching notes;
- verify datasets, figures, and relative paths;
- render and test the complete session.

Commit completed sessions separately, for example:

```text
Port Session 4 regression materials to R
```

### Stage 4: Standardize course infrastructure

After the content migration:

- standardize exercise assignment/solution profiles;
- instead of `.ipynb` output, use `.qmd` and knitr (provide a corresponding introductory explanation);
- remove obsolete Python/Jupyter/Codespaces instructions;
- update links, survey variables, metadata, and course references;
- verify the full course render and session overview.

:::
